background.zh: 《世界末日的菌菇》跟随松茸从美国俄勒冈的森林，经日本的分级市场，到中国云南与芬兰的采集地。松茸无法人工栽培，只能在被人类扰动过的松林里生长；它因此成为一条理想的线索，把资本主义废墟、多物种生计与全球贸易串在一起。Tsing 与「松茸世界研究组」的同事一起追踪采集者、中间商、买家、科学家与森林管理者，提出「拾荒式积累」：资本不是从废墟之外到来，而是靠废墟中的残余继续积累。
background.en: The Mushroom at the End of the World follows matsutake from Oregon forests through Japanese grading markets to gathering sites in Yunnan and Finland. Matsutake cannot be cultivated and grows only in human-disturbed pine forests, making it an ideal thread through capitalist ruins, multispecies livelihoods and global trade. With the Matsutake Worlds Research Group, Tsing tracks gatherers, brokers, buyers, scientists and forest managers, and proposes 'salvage accumulation': capital does not arrive from outside the ruins but keeps accumulating through what the ruins leave behind.

narrative.zh: 全书由可独立成章的田野片段组成，分成「残余」「进步者」「扰动」「机会」「废墟」五个运动。每一部分换一个尺度：森林生态、采集者的生计、分级市场、全球供应链、以及「世界末日」作为一种生活条件。Tsing 不追求一条直线论证，而是让概念在反复出现的场景中显形：同一朵松茸，在不同人手里是礼物、商品、物种伙伴与废墟的征兆。
narrative.en: The book is built from field fragments that can stand alone, arranged in five movements: what's left, progressor, disturbance, opportunity and ruins. Each shifts scale: forest ecology, gatherers' livelihoods, grading markets, global supply chains, and the end of the world as a condition of life. Tsing does not pursue a straight line; concepts emerge through recurring scenes in which the same mushroom is gift, commodity, species partner and symptom of ruin.

intent.reception_good_zh: 出版后成为多物种研究与人类世讨论的核心文本；「拾荒式积累」「潜在公共领域」「注意的艺术」被广泛引用，也让松茸成为跨学科课堂的常见案例。
intent.reception_good_en: It became a central text in multispecies studies and Anthropocene debates; salvage accumulation, latent commons and arts of noticing are widely cited, and matsutake became a staple classroom case.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 评论也提出：本书对资本主义结构的批判有时被民族志的丰富性稀释；「废墟中的希望」容易被读成一种浪漫化的生存美学。
intent.reception_bad_en: Reviews also suggested that the critique of capitalist structure is sometimes diluted by ethnographic richness, and that 'hope in ruins' can be read as a romantic aesthetics of survival.
intent.syn_zh: 本书的贡献不是证明废墟中有希望，而是展示「在废墟中生活」的具体条件：多物种协作、拾荒式积累、以及不被承认的公共资源。
intent.syn_en: The contribution is not to prove that there is hope in ruins but to show the concrete conditions of living in them: multispecies collaboration, salvage accumulation and unrecognised commons.

reception.then_zh: 2015 年出版后迅速成为多物种研究与人类世讨论的核心文本，并进入大量跨学科课程。评论普遍肯定其民族志想象力与概念创造力。
reception.then_en: Published in 2015, it quickly became a core text in multispecies studies and Anthropocene debates and entered many interdisciplinary syllabi. Reviews generally praised its ethnographic imagination and conceptual invention.
reception.later_zh: 「拾荒式积累」被用于废弃物、供应链、修复与基础设施研究；「注意的艺术」成为环境人文的方法口号之一。
reception.later_en: Salvage accumulation travelled into studies of waste, supply chains, repair and infrastructure; arts of noticing became a methodological slogan in environmental humanities.
reception.influence_zh: 本书让松茸成为全球供应链研究的经典案例，也让「多物种」从理论口号变成可操作的田野方法。
reception.influence_en: The book made matsutake a classic case in supply-chain studies and turned multispecies from a slogan into a workable field method.
reception.critique_zh: 主要保留是：对资本积累的整体结构批判不足；「废墟中的希望」可能美化 precarious 生计；案例的全球跨度也带来比较方法上的不对称。
reception.critique_en: The main reservations are that the critique of capital accumulation is underdeveloped, 'hope in ruins' may aestheticise precarious livelihoods, and the global span produces asymmetries of comparison.

author_intent.claim_en: Tsing wants to show that capitalist ruins are not the end of life but the condition of multispecies collaborative survival; that survival is not triumph but something that happens together with salvage accumulation, contamination and precarity.
author_intent.why_zh: 书名把「世界末日」与「生命可能性」并置，拒绝末日论也拒绝进步论；选择松茸，是因为它无法被完全栽培、只能在扰动过的森林生长，正好承载「废墟中的生命」；全书以「注意的艺术」开篇，说明方法本身就是要看见被结构分析忽略的生命。
author_intent.why_en: The title pairs the end of the world with the possibility of life, refusing both doom and progress; matsutake is chosen because it cannot be fully cultivated and grows only in disturbed forests, carrying 'life in ruins'; the book opens with arts of noticing, making method itself a way to see life that structural analysis misses.

review.title_zh: 在废墟里注意：读《世界末日的菌菇》
review.standfirst_zh: 资本主义废墟不是终点，而是多物种协作生存的条件——但这不是一个温暖的故事。
review.standfirst_en: Capitalist ruins are not an endpoint but the condition of multispecies survival — and this is not a warm story.
review.body_zh:
《世界末日的菌菇》有一个容易被误读的书名。它不预言世界末日，也不承诺废墟中的救赎；它说的是：世界末日已经以不均匀的方式发生，而生命仍在其中继续。松茸是这条论证最好的载体——它无法被栽培，只能在被砍伐、被耕作、被遗弃的松林里生长；它的供应链把俄勒冈的采集者、日本的买家、云南的村庄与芬兰的森林连在一起。

Tsing 的方法不是从结构开始，而是从「注意」开始。她先让你看见一朵松茸如何被不同的人手触碰、分级、定价，再让你看见这些动作背后的资本主义废墟。拾荒式积累、潜在公共领域、多物种生计，这些概念不是抽象的口号，而是从具体场景里长出来的。

这本书的力量也带来风险：当「废墟中的生命」被写得如此丰富时，读者容易忘记废墟本身是被制造出来的，也容易把 precarious 生计浪漫化。Tsing 自己并不回避剥削，但她的笔触更偏向生命的韧性，而不是结构的暴力。

读它最好的方式，是同时保持两种注意：注意松茸、采集者与森林的协作；也注意让他们处于废墟中的权力关系。只有两种注意同时在场，这本书才不会被读成一碗温暖的汤。
review.abstract_en:
The Mushroom at the End of the World has a title that invites misreading. It neither predicts the end nor promises salvation in ruins; it says that the end of the world is already happening unevenly, and that life continues within it. Matsutake is the perfect carrier: it cannot be cultivated and grows only in logged, cultivated and abandoned pine forests; its supply chain links Oregon gatherers, Japanese buyers, Yunnan villages and Finnish forests.

Tsing's method starts not from structure but from noticing. She first lets you see how a mushroom is touched, graded and priced by different hands, then lets you see the capitalist ruins behind those gestures. Salvage accumulation, latent commons and multispecies livelihoods are not abstract slogans but concepts grown from concrete scenes.

The book's strength brings a risk: when life in ruins is written so richly, readers may forget that the ruins are made, and may romanticise precarious livelihoods. Tsing does not avoid exploitation, but her prose leans toward the resilience of life rather than the violence of structure.

The best way to read it is to hold two kinds of attention at once: attention to the collaboration of mushroom, gatherer and forest, and attention to the power relations that keep them in ruins. Only with both does the book avoid becoming a warm bowl of soup.

background.zh: 《在受损星球上生活的艺术》由 Tsing 与 Nils Bubandt、Elaine Gan、Heather Anne Swanson 合编，源自一次关于人类世与多物种生活的跨学科会议。全书分「幽灵」（Ghosts）与「怪物」（Monsters）两部分：幽灵指过去暴力与毒性留下的长期遗产，怪物指新出现的、跨物种的混合体。编者要问的不是「如何拯救地球」，而是「在已经受损的星球上，如何学习共同生活」。
background.en: Arts of Living on a Damaged Planet is edited by Tsing with Nils Bubandt, Elaine Gan and Heather Anne Swanson, growing out of an interdisciplinary conference on the Anthropocene and multispecies life. It is divided into 'Ghosts' and 'Monsters': ghosts are the long legacies of past violence and toxicity, monsters are emergent cross-species assemblages. The editors ask not how to save the earth but how to learn to live together on an already damaged planet.

narrative.zh: 这不是一部单作者专著，而是一部编排过的文集：两部分各自收录人类学、生物学、艺术史与环境研究的文章，彼此之间以短评与图像连接。「幽灵」部分从毒性、殖民暴力与物种灭绝的遗留写起；「怪物」部分从杂交、共生与新生态组合写起。两种写法共同拒绝「人类世」作为单一整体，强调其不均匀、可感知、可讲述的局部。
narrative.en: This is not a single-author monograph but an edited collection: each part gathers essays from anthropology, biology, art history and environmental studies, linked by short commentaries and images. 'Ghosts' begins from the legacies of toxicity, colonial violence and extinction; 'Monsters' begins from hybridity, symbiosis and new ecological assemblages. Together they refuse the Anthropocene as a single whole and stress its uneven, perceptible, tellable localities.

intent.reception_bad_en: As an edited collection, the chapters vary in quality and theoretical density, and the ghosts/monsters binary has been criticised as too neat.

review.title_zh: 与幽灵和怪物共处：读《在受损星球上生活的艺术》
review.standfirst_zh: 人类世不是整体，而是由过去的幽灵与新生的怪物共同构成的斑驳现场。
review.standfirst_en: The Anthropocene is not a whole but a patchy field of past ghosts and emergent monsters.
review.body_zh:
《在受损星球上生活的艺术》首先是一部编排之书。它不试图用一篇导论解释人类世，而是把不同学科的文章放进「幽灵」与「怪物」两个房间：前者回望毒性、殖民暴力与灭绝的遗留，后者前瞻杂交、共生与新生态组合。读者在两部分之间来回，逐渐感到「人类世」不是一个时代，而是一组不均匀的伤口与生长。

这种编排有明确的方法论意图：如果人类世是斑驳的，那么单一尺度的解决方案就是错位的。本书因此不提供全球治理方案，只提供局部的注意技艺——如何看见毒性的长期作用，如何讲述一个新物种的出现，如何在受损的地方继续生活。

局限也很明显：文集各章质量不一，「幽灵/怪物」的二分有时过于文学化，可能遮蔽具体的政治经济差异。它更适合被当作一套感知训练，而不是一部人类世总论。

读它最好的方式，是把它与《菌菇》对读：一个从废墟中的生计出发，一个从受损星球的多重时间出发。两者合起来，才是 Tsing 的多物种世界。
review.abstract_en:
Arts of Living on a Damaged Planet is first an edited book. It does not try to explain the Anthropocene in one introduction; it places essays from different disciplines in two rooms, ghosts and monsters: the first looks back at toxicity, colonial violence and extinction, the second looks forward to hybridity, symbiosis and new ecological assemblages. Moving between them, the reader comes to feel that the Anthropocene is not an era but a set of uneven wounds and growths.

The arrangement has a methodological point: if the Anthropocene is patchy, single-scale solutions are mismatched. The book therefore offers no global governance plan, only local arts of noticing — how to see the long action of toxicity, how to narrate the arrival of a new species, how to keep living in a damaged place.

The limits are clear: the chapters vary in quality, and the ghosts/monsters binary can be too literary, obscuring concrete political-economic differences. It is better used as a training in perception than as a general theory of the Anthropocene.

The best way to read it is alongside Mushroom: one starts from livelihood in ruins, the other from the multiple temporalities of a damaged planet. Together they form Tsing's multispecies world.

background.zh: Feral Atlas 是一个数字项目（feralatlas.org），由 Tsing、Jennifer Deger、Alder Keleman Saxena 与 Feifei Zhou 合编。它收集「野性」的田野报告：工业基础设施、殖民农业、水坝、港口与军事基地如何产生超出设计意图的生态后果。项目以互动地图、短文、图像与声音组织材料，让读者在具体地点追踪「超越人类的人类世」。它不是一本纸质书，而是一个可探索的公共知识平台。
background.en: Feral Atlas is a digital project (feralatlas.org) edited by Tsing, Jennifer Deger, Alder Keleman Saxena and Feifei Zhou. It gathers field reports of the 'feral': how industrial infrastructure, colonial agriculture, dams, ports and military bases produce ecological consequences beyond their design. Interactive maps, short essays, images and sound let readers track the more-than-human Anthropocene in specific places. It is not a print book but an explorable public knowledge platform.

narrative.zh: 项目以「田野报告」为基本单位，每个报告从一个具体基础设施或地点出发，追踪其野性后果，再通过地图与标签与其他报告连接。读者不按线性章节阅读，而是在地点、物种、基础设施类型之间跳转。Tsing 的导论把「野性」定义为「人类活动引发、却超出人类控制的生命后果」，并说明为什么数字平台比纸质书更适合呈现这种多线索、多尺度的材料。
narrative.en: The project's basic unit is the field report: each starts from a specific infrastructure or site, traces its feral consequences, and connects to other reports through maps and tags. Readers do not follow linear chapters but move among places, species and infrastructure types. Tsing's introduction defines the feral as 'life consequences set off by human activity but beyond human control' and explains why a digital platform suits this multi-threaded, multi-scale material better than print.

intent.reception_good_en: Since launch it has been treated as a landmark of digital environmental humanities, often read with Mushroom and the Field Guide; it made 'feral' a common term for the ecological afterlives of infrastructure.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 作为数字项目，它的可访问性、长期维护与引用稳定性都受到限制；「野性」也可能被读成一种审美化的越界。
intent.reception_bad_en: As a digital project it faces limits of access, long-term maintenance and citational stability; 'feral' can also be read as an aestheticised transgression.
intent.syn_zh: Feral Atlas 的贡献是把「人类世」从全球模型变成可点击的地点：每一个野性后果都可以被追踪到具体的基础设施与生命。
intent.syn_en: The contribution is to turn the Anthropocene from a global model into clickable places: every feral consequence can be traced to specific infrastructure and life.

review.title_zh: 可点击的人类世：读 Feral Atlas
review.standfirst_zh: 把「人类世」从全球模型变成可点击的地点：每一个野性后果都能被追踪到具体的基础设施与生命。
review.standfirst_en: Turning the Anthropocene from a global model into clickable places: every feral consequence can be traced to specific infrastructure and life.
review.body_zh:
Feral Atlas 最激进的地方不是它的内容，而是它的形式。它拒绝把人类世写成一本从第一章读到最后一章的书，而是让读者在地图、物种与基础设施之间跳转。每一个「田野报告」都从一个具体地点出发：一座水坝、一片种植园、一个港口、一处军事基地。报告追踪的不是「自然被破坏」，而是「人类活动产生了什么超出控制的生命后果」。

这种形式与论点是一致的：如果人类世是斑驳的、多线索的，那么知识形态也应该是斑驳的、多入口的。Tsing 与编者把「野性」定义为人类活动引发却超出人类控制的生命后果，这个定义既避免了「自然 vs 人类」的二分，也避免了把一切后果都归给资本的简化。

局限也来自形式：数字项目的可访问性与长期维护不稳定，引用与教学使用都比纸质书困难；「野性」的扩散叙事也可能淡化具体公司与国家的责任。它更像一个可探索的公共档案，而不是一部完整的理论著作。

把它与《野外指南》对读，会看见 Tsing 的方法在两种媒介之间的迁移：数字平台让材料可探索，纸质指南让方法可携带。两者都不是终点，而是同一场「注意」训练的不同工具。
review.abstract_en:
Feral Atlas is most radical not in its content but in its form. It refuses to write the Anthropocene as a book read from first chapter to last, letting readers jump among maps, species and infrastructure. Each field report starts from a specific site: a dam, a plantation, a port, a military base. What it traces is not 'nature being destroyed' but 'what life consequences human activity sets off beyond control'.

The form matches the argument: if the Anthropocene is patchy and multi-threaded, knowledge should also be patchy and multi-entry. Tsing and the editors define the feral as life consequences set off by human activity but beyond human control, avoiding both the nature/human binary and the reduction of all consequences to capital.

The limits come from the form: digital access and long-term maintenance are unstable, citation and teaching are harder than with print, and the diffuse narrative of the feral can underplay the responsibility of specific firms and states. It is more an explorable public archive than a complete theoretical work.

Read alongside the Field Guide, it shows Tsing's method migrating between media: the digital platform makes material explorable, the printed guide makes the method portable. Neither is an endpoint; both are tools in the same training of attention.

background.zh: 《斑驳人类世野外指南》由 Tsing、Jennifer Deger、Alder Keleman Saxena 与 Feifei Zhou 合著，2024 年出版。它把《野性图谱》的数字材料转写为一本可携带的「野外指南」：不是教你识别鸟兽，而是教你识别「斑块」——人类活动、基础设施与非人类生命密集交织的具体地点。书的核心主张是：人类世不是全球均匀的整体，而是由无数不同步、不连续的斑块拼成。
background.en: Field Guide to the Patchy Anthropocene, co-authored by Tsing, Jennifer Deger, Alder Keleman Saxena and Feifei Zhou and published in 2024, rewrites the digital material of Feral Atlas into a portable field guide. It does not teach you to identify birds or plants but to identify patches: concrete sites where human activity, infrastructure and nonhuman life are densely intertwined. Its core claim is that the Anthropocene is not a globally even whole but a composition of countless non-synchronous, discontinuous patches.

narrative.zh: 全书以「指南」而非「专著」的形式组织：概念条目、案例斑块、图像与阅读路线交错。它先解释「斑驳人类世」是什么，再给出识别斑块的工具（注意、追踪、比较），最后把工具放回具体地点。读者可以按顺序读，也可以像使用野外指南一样，按地点或主题跳读。
narrative.en: The book is organised as a guide rather than a monograph: conceptual entries, case patches, images and reading routes interlace. It first explains what the patchy Anthropocene is, then offers tools for identifying patches (noticing, tracing, comparing), and finally returns the tools to concrete sites. Readers can go in order or, like a field guide, jump by site or theme.

intent.reception_bad_en: Reviews also suggested that the guide form can make the argument feel fragmentary, and that the patch concept needs clearer boundaries when used across scales.

review.title_zh: 把人类世装进口袋：读《斑驳人类世野外指南》
review.standfirst_zh: 人类世不是整体，而是由不同步的斑块拼成；理解它需要一套可携带的注意技艺。
review.standfirst_en: The Anthropocene is not a whole but a composition of non-synchronous patches; understanding it requires a portable craft of noticing.
review.body_zh:
《斑驳人类世野外指南》是一本奇怪的书：它把「人类世」这样的大词，写成了一本可以随身携带的指南。它不教你识别鸟兽，而是教你识别「斑块」——那些人类活动、基础设施与非人类生命密集交织的具体地点。它的核心主张很简单，也很难做到：不要从「全球」开始，从你能看见的斑块开始。

这种形式不是装饰。如果人类世是不同步的、不连续的，那么一本线性的总论就会错过它的对象。指南的条目化、可跳读、可携带，正是为了让你在不同的斑块之间移动，并逐渐看见它们之间的差异与联系。

局限也来自形式：条目化可能削弱论证的连贯性，「斑块」的边界在跨尺度使用时并不清楚，案例选择也可能偏向作者熟悉的地区。它更像一套训练工具，而不是一部完整的人类世理论。

把它与《菌菇》对读，会看见 Tsing 的方法从「废墟」走向「斑块」：前者强调时间与生计，后者强调空间与注意。两者都不是答案，而是让你重新学会看世界的方式。
review.abstract_en:
Field Guide to the Patchy Anthropocene is an odd book: it turns a large term, the Anthropocene, into a guide you can carry. It does not teach you to identify birds or plants but to identify patches — concrete sites where human activity, infrastructure and nonhuman life are densely intertwined. Its core claim is simple and hard to practise: do not start from the global; start from a patch you can see.

The form is not decoration. If the Anthropocene is non-synchronous and discontinuous, a linear overview will miss its object. The guide's entries, skippability and portability are meant to let you move among patches and gradually see their differences and connections.

The limits come from the form: entry-based writing can weaken coherence, the boundaries of a patch are unclear across scales, and case selection may favour regions familiar to the authors. It is more a training kit than a complete theory of the Anthropocene.

Read alongside Mushroom, it shows Tsing's method moving from ruins to patches: the former stresses time and livelihood, the latter space and attention. Neither is an answer; both retrain how you see the world.
